messages:
support-bot: New inbound from Sales — two tickets that look related: INC-4872 (AcmeCorp) and INC-4879 (Stellar Tech). Both mention per-tenant embedding rate limits + 429s during bursts. Flagging for product triage.

olivia: thanks. linking here. quick ask — do we treat these as duplicates or separate product asks (rate-limit increase vs dashboard visibility)? :thinking_face:

kai: initial skim: both mention same root cause (burst QPS, KV cache miss). Customer contexts differ (Acme has steady stream, Stellar has spiky bursts). Could be same backlog item with different acceptance criteria.

marco: agree with kai. propose flow: 1) create canonical intake card in Jira (FEATURE-2213) 2) tag incoming tickets with "intake:customer-request" + "intake:possible-duplicate:FEATURE-2213" 3) owner does quick scoping and notes differences.

olivia: ok i'll create the canonical card and add a short scope block. can someone volunteer to own outreach to both customers for clarifying traffic patterns? we should avoid assuming identical SLO needs.

emily: I can reach out to Acme (INC-4872) today. I'll use the standard intake template and ask for: p95/p99 QPS, sample request rates, whether they have burst windows, and config (batching/quantization).

marco: I'll take Stellar (INC-4879). I'll ask for their SDK version and if they use our hosted API or Dedicated. That will affect the mitigation path.

kai: For prioritization: propose tagging canonical card with severity and impact notes like "impact:high-customer-dollar" or "impact:multiple-customers". Also add a triage score field with components: revenue, unblock-customer, engineering-effort. 1-10 scale.

olivia: +1 on triage score. I'll add a short rubric to FEATURE-2213 so triage is reproducible. Template fields: summary, reproduction steps, customers impacted, tentative solution(s), rollback plan, acceptance criteria.

support-bot: Noted: INC-4872 and INC-4879 now reference FEATURE-2213 via tag "intake:canonical:FEATURE-2213".

emily: Drafting status reply for Acme — please review before I send: "Hi Sam — thanks for the report. We've consolidated your ticket into FEATURE-2213 for tracking. To help prioritize, could you share recent p95/p99 request rates and any burst examples (timestamps)? We'll follow up with a targeted mitigation plan once we confirm traffic patterns." Thoughts?

marco: looks good. suggest adding "expected impact if we don't change" line so they can call out customer-visible pain. e.g., "Are customers seeing failures or timeouts? If so, how often?"

olivia: final note for backlog grooming: let's schedule a 30-min intake sync tomorrow 11am PT to finalize acceptance criteria and initial effort estimate. Agenda: 1) confirm duplicates vs variants 2) decide quick mitigations (rate-limit overrides / caching) 3) assign engineering owner for spike.

kai: added to my calendar. tagging: please use labels: customer:acme, customer:stellar, intake:needs-info, triage:investigating. Keep the canonical card description small — link to tickets for full convo.

emily: sending Acme reply now. I'll include a note that we'll update them once FEATURE-2213 moves to planning and provide expected timeline (TBD).

olivia: thanks team. once we have responses, we'll either: A) mark as duplicate and leave FEATURE-2213 single implementation with per-customer acceptance tests or B) split into 2213-A/2213-B if solutions diverge. I'll update the customers accordingly. :thumbsup:
